output.name: Kavesk
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up but did not come all the way free. A short length of cord stayed knotted to his hand, and it still hangs at the bottom of the Unflown, trailing down past everything else. Mother Hesk counted the turns on her Reel and found one missing, and she has never forgiven the wind for it. The Ray That Flies, who saw the Gale take Hanur's son out past the rocks, hangs above it to the north and watches the cord swing. The Cliff Ladder, to the west, did not go up with the sky; it still hangs on its nail with Ennu's whale-rib rungs. Tavo laughs when he passes, and he cannot be asked to tie it back. Sailors lost in fog are told to follow the cord, for it runs toward where the string was cut. Ennu says a cut kite can be mended, though Ennu says many things over a needle. Sil looks along that cord every night for her brother, and finds only the hanging end.
output.finding: Sailors far south should find the Ray That Flies and then look three-quarters of a hand-span due south of her, where the Cut End hangs at the tail of its loose cord.
